name: Commanders
subhead: 2026 training camp edition — two first-time coordinators, $100M spent on the edge, and a healthy Jayden Daniels asked to run a different offense.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Both coordinators replaced. Quinn promoted assistant QB coach David Blough to offensive coordinator (Kliff Kingsbury left for the Rams) and hired ex-Vikings pass game coordinator Daronte Jones as DC, replacing Joe Whitt Jr.

Two first-time NFL play-callers. Neither Blough nor Jones has called plays in the league; Jones has one year of coordinator experience at LSU. National coverage has framed these as genuine gambles — Quinn has publicly stood firm on both.
RumorQuinn's own seat. After a 5–12 collapse, hot-seat chatter has followed him into camp. A third straight uneven season with hand-picked, unproven coordinators would be difficult to explain.
The scheme shift. Blough's offense leans on more under-center play-action — a real departure from the shotgun-heavy attack Daniels ran as a rookie.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedOdafe Oweh, EDGE — four years, $100M. The largest commitment of the offseason and the anchor of a rebuilt pass rush.
SignedDT Tim Settle Jr. (3 yr / $24M), LB Leo Chenal, S Nick Cross, CB Amik Robertson; EDGE Dorance Armstrong brought back.
SignedTE Chig Okonkwo and RB Rachaad White; WR Treylon Burks re-signed.
DraftWR Antonio Williams added to a receiver room that needed young legs.
LostWR Deebo Samuel allowed to walk after one season; RB Austin Ekeler not re-signed; TE Zach Ertz departed.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Jayden Daniels, QB. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year lost 2025 to a cascade of injuries — knee sprain, hamstring strain, and a dislocated elbow that ended his season. He played only four full games. Spring and summer reports have been encouraging: comfortable, moving well, back in sync with Terry McLaurin.
The adjustment. Daniels' transition to Blough's under-center, play-action-heavy system is the single most important variable in Washington's season.
Odafe Oweh, EDGE. $100M says the pass rush is now his responsibility. Paired with Armstrong and Settle inside, the front is unrecognizable from 2025.
Terry McLaurin, WR. Still the offense's anchor, and the chemistry reports with a healthy Daniels are the most positive signal out of the spring.
Receiver room, reset. With Samuel gone, rookie Antonio Williams and re-signed Treylon Burks compete for snaps behind McLaurin.
Backfield, reset. Rachaad White replaces Ekeler as the veteran presence.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Washington's 2025 was a health story disguised as a collapse — four full games from Jayden Daniels and a 5–12 finish. The fix was money on defense (Oweh's $100M leading a rebuilt front) and a philosophical reset on offense. The risk is concentrated in one place: Dan Quinn handed both play-calling jobs to men who have never held them in the NFL, in a year his own seat is being discussed. A healthy Daniels makes it look bold. Anything less makes it look like the last decision he gets to make.
